# @@project_id is the read-only ID of the project that runs the query, test, in a single
# statement as in a script; inside a procedure it is still the project that runs the script.
# third_party/bigquery_docs/reference/system-variables.md

SELECT @@project_id
=> "test"

# Answers collected from BigQuery with bqanswers: system variable names are case-insensitive.
SELECT @@PROJECT_ID = @@project_id
=> "true"

SELECT 1;
SELECT @@project_id
=> "test"

# Setting @@dataset_project_id changes name resolution, not the executing project.
SET @@dataset_project_id = 'example-project';
SELECT @@project_id
=> "test"

# INFORMATION_SCHEMA names the project by its ID.
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM `region-us`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SCHEMATA WHERE catalog_name = @@project_id AND schema_name = "scalars"
=> "1"

SELECT LOGICAL_AND(table_catalog = @@project_id) FROM scalars.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES WHERE table_name = "t"
=> "true"

CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE scalars.proc_project_id() OPTIONS(strict_mode=FALSE)
BEGIN SELECT @@project_id; END;
CALL scalars.proc_project_id()
=> "test"
